premises.title: The Keeper
premises.opening_image: A lighthouse on a black rock in a storm, its beam sweeping an empty sea; a small keeper in a yellow oilskin turns the lamp by hand.
premises.audience_hook: What is the huge dark shape the beam just caught under the waves, and will she hide the light?
premises.central_action: The keeper tracks a giant shape with a glinting eye as it closes on the rock, starts to shutter the lamp to hide, hears it moan, and instead turns the full beam onto it.
premises.complication: Every clue (the swell, the size of its shadow in the lightning, the moan) says monster, and hiding is the safe choice.
premises.payoff: A whale calf surfaces in the beam, small and crying; she swings the light out to sea, a vast tail rises where it ends, and the calf swims home. At dawn two spouts rise from a sea that was never empty.
premises.art_motion_idea: Painterly chiaroscuro: a dark teal storm lit only by the beam and lightning, parallax wave layers, rain, film grain; slow suspense pacing and a light that acts.
premises.library_fit: Nothing in Classic: no sea, weather, light cones, creature or new character; built new.

premises.title: Repair Call
premises.opening_image: A tiny repair technician squeezes through a hatch into a warm, humming machine room full of pipes.
premises.central_action: The technician tightens valves while the pipes swell and sigh and a round gauge blinks.
premises.complication: Each repair makes the machine hum louder, as if waking.
premises.payoff: Pulling back reveals the machine is a sleeping dragon and the gauge is its eye, which winks and goes back to sleep.
premises.art_motion_idea: Interior cutaway with warm lights and a big pull-back reveal.
premises.library_fit: Would need a new interior and creature; no Classic overlap.

premises.title: Last Train
premises.opening_image: An empty night platform; one passenger waits under a flickering lamp, clutching a ticket.
premises.audience_hook: Who is the passenger waiting for on a platform with no trains?
premises.central_action: Lights of an approaching train grow, the passenger stands, the train passes without stopping.
premises.complication: The ticket is for a date long gone.
premises.payoff: The passenger turns and finds an old friend who has been waiting on the bench all along.
premises.art_motion_idea: Lamp-lit quiet scene, slow pans, mostly stillness.

rationale: The Keeper has a reveal that recasts everything before it (the threat was a child), a choice the character makes on screen (hide or shine), and an environment that does story work: the beam is both what finds the 'monster' and what brings it home, and the storm clearing is the emotional release. Repair Call's reveal is a twist without a choice; Last Train is quieter and depends on backstory a 30-second film cannot carry.
